title: Google Business Profile Messaging Is Back, and AI Answers First
html:
Google Business Profile messaging is coming back, and this time an AI agent answers customers for you. Search Engine Roundtable reported on October 29, 2026 that Google is opening an early-access pilot to more businesses. Customers tap a button in Search or Maps and chat from their phone's own messaging app. See also the Google Maps message button that now sits next to Call on Android and iOS.

Google has not posted a public announcement yet, so treat the details as early reports, not final rules. For a home service business, the safe move is to get your profile data clean before the agent starts quoting it.

Source: Search Engine Roundtable: Google Business Profiles AI-Powered Messaging Expands, published October 29, 2026.

  • The pilot is invite-only and free for now, and Google has not shared a rollout date.
  • The agent answers routine questions from your profile and hands off anything it cannot handle.
  • It works only for customers on RCS-capable phones and carriers.
  • Wrong hours, service areas or categories on your profile become wrong answers in the chat.

What is Google Business Profile messaging now?

It is a chat button on your listing that lets a searcher message you without leaving Google. The reply comes from an AI agent first, and you can step in at any point. Messages show up inside your profile, and a red dot marks new ones.

Think of it as a front desk that works at 11 p.m. and reads only from what you have posted online.

Did Google drop chat before?

Yes. Google shut off native Business Profile chat in the summer of 2024. According to Silverfox Digital, new chats stopped on July 15, 2024, and the feature was fully gone by July 31.

The comeback surfaced in a short slip in June 2026. Search Engine Roundtable noted on June 26 that a messages area labeled "Handled by your AI agent" appeared for a few hours and then vanished. The October invitations suggest Google kept building.

How does the AI agent work, and where does it stop?

The agent reads your listing, answers the simple stuff and passes the rest to you. Hours, service areas and basic "do you work on this" questions are its sweet spot. A quote request or a messy job description goes to a person.

Two limits matter. First, it needs RCS, so a customer on an older setup just sends you a normal text. Second, Digitaleo's guide points out that answer quality depends on how accurate your listing is.

Where the chat ends up Who handles it What you control
Hours, service area, basic services AI agent Profile accuracy
Quote or estimate request You or your office Response time
Emergency or same-day job You, by phone Call routing
Customer without RCS You, by plain text Phone coverage

Who is likely to handle each type of chat, based on early reports of the pilot.

Mistake to avoid: assuming the agent books jobs for you. Reports so far describe answers and handoffs, with reservations shown only in a restaurant example.

Why does this matter for a home service business?

Because a homeowner with a leaking pipe messages three companies and picks whoever answers first. An invite-only chat button is one more place where that race happens, before your website ever loads.

A trade vendor backs up the speed point. That is a vendor survey, so read it as direction, not law.

What happens when the agent repeats bad profile data?

It repeats it with confidence. If your listing says you close at 5 p.m. and you now run emergency calls until 9, the agent tells the customer you are closed.

Profile field How it fails in chat Quick fix
Hours Agent says closed during emergency hours Add special and holiday hours
Service area Agent turns away a town you cover Match the area to your real map
Categories Agent denies a service you offer Add every service as a category or service line
Phone number Handoff goes to a dead line Test the number on a Saturday

What should a contractor do this week?

Fix the data, then fix the handoff. You do not need the feature to start doing either.

How does chat fit with Google Ads and Local Services Ads?

Google is pushing chat across ads and organic results, not only profiles. The same PPC Land report says Invoca launched a beta messaging agent that answers and books from chats started in Google Search, and feeds sales outcomes into Google Ads to guide bids.

For a paid program, this means tracking chats as leads. Your Google Ads management setup should count a booked chat the same way it counts a booked call.

What should you ignore for now?

Skip any pitch that sells "AI messaging setup" as if the feature were live for everyone. It is an invite-only pilot, and Google has not documented it.

Also skip rebuilding your site around chat. A fast home service website with a clear call button still wins the customer who does not use RCS.

Electrical

Electricians field "is this safe" questions the agent should hand off fast.

Is Google Business Profile messaging available to everyone?

No. Reports describe an invite-only pilot, mostly in the United States, and Google has not shared a public timeline. Check your dashboard for a new Messages button, and keep answering calls and texts the usual way until Google confirms a wider rollout for all businesses.

Does the AI agent cost anything?

Reports say the agent answers routine questions for free during the pilot. Customers whose phones lack RCS send a plain text instead, and standard texting rates may apply to them. Google has not published pricing, so expect terms to change once the pilot ends or expands.

What is RCS, and why does it matter here?

RCS is an upgraded text messaging standard built into many newer phones and carrier networks. The agent works only when the customer has it. Everyone else sends a plain text straight to your phone, so your own reply speed still matters for those leads.

How is this different from the chat Google removed in 2024?

The old feature was a basic inbox that Google shut down in July 2024. The new version puts an AI agent in front, answers common questions from your profile, and passes harder requests to you. Customers chat from their phone messaging app instead of a Google inbox.

Sources

  • Search Engine Roundtable: Google Business Profiles AI-Powered Messaging Expands, October 29, 2026
  • Search Engine Roundtable: Google Business Profile Message Button, June 26, 2026
  • PPC Land: Invoca AI agents book appointments from chats started in Google Search, October 28, 2026
  • Silverfox Digital: Google Business Profile AI Message Feature: What Local Businesses Need to Know, undated
  • Digitaleo: Google Business Profile: Everything to Know About the Return of AI-Powered Messaging, undated
